name: The builders of Babel
charge: Building a tower to make themselves a name and resist being scattered
summary: The whole earth was of one language and one speech, and journeying from the east they found a plain in the land of Shinar and dwelt there. They said, let us build us a city and a tower whose top may reach unto heaven, and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth. The Lord came down, confounded their language, and scattered them.
offense: The builders at Shinar shared one language and proposed a city and a tower, naming their purpose themselves: make us a name, lest we be scattered over the earth (Genesis 11:1-4). Their unity was directed toward securing their own name and resisting dispersion. This stands against the charge to Noah's sons to be fruitful, multiply, and replenish the earth (Genesis 9:1). The Lord saw the people as one, with one language, and declared that nothing would be restrained from what they imagined to do (Genesis 11:6). Agreement alone was no proof of righteousness. The people could combine skill and labour while pursuing an end contrary to God's ordering. Nimrod's kingdom began in Babel and the same land of Shinar (Genesis 10:8-10); the name and place belong to the growth of human power, not an authority above God's judgment.
judgment: The Lord confounded their language so that they could not understand one another's speech, scattered them upon the earth, and they left off building the city (Genesis 11:7-9). The sentence brought about the very dispersion they had resolved to prevent. The tower could not secure its builders against the will of God.

entries.commentary: The whole earth was of one language, and they journeyed from the east to the plain of Shinar. Coming from Jerusalem eastward lands you in Shinar, in Babylon. They built the tower so they would not be scattered abroad; the fear of the flood was still on them, and they wanted to make themselves a name.

The people being one was not going to produce righteousness; nothing would be restrained from what they imagined to do, and it would be evil, so the Most High confounded their language and scattered them. There has never been a doctrine of all nations holding hands as one in the scriptures. The Most High divided the nations their inheritance and separated the sons of Adam, setting the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. The man of sin opposes this: he exalts himself above all that is called God, gathers all nations to himself as one, and deifies himself, making God and the Messiah after his own image. That is the same thing Nimrod did in the land of Shinar. After Babel the Most High sent every family back to where it was supposed to be: Ham to his place, Shem to his, Japheth to his.

Watch the lifespans in the generations of Shem: five hundred years, then four hundred, then two hundred, then down past one hundred and nineteen with Nahor. The word of [Genesis 6:3](/bible/genesis/6#v3) is taking hold on man's days. Each of these generations begat sons and daughters for hundreds of years; the earth is being populated again all through this chapter.

Haran begat Lot and died before his father Terah in Ur of the Chaldees. Ur means fire in the etymology, and the Chaldees is Babylon; Abram was born and called out of that area. Lot was a just man. To be just means to do that which is lawful and right, a commandment keeper; righteous Lot was vexed from day to day with the unlawful deeds of the wicked.
Noah and his sons were told to replenish the earth after the flood, and the earth is replenished with righteous children; a multitude of ungodly children profits nothing.
The fear and dread of man upon the beasts is not how it was in the beginning, and not how it will remain; the original relationship between man and the animals will be restored.

This is the introduction of man eating meat. The Most High did not give man a new stomach; the body was already made for it and it lay dormant until after the flood. Having the liberty to eat meat does not mean eating without balance; be not too greedy upon meats, for excess of meats brings sickness. The law of what may be eaten was already understood; you could not eat everything. The doctrine that says you can pray over anything and eat it is a seducing spirit and a doctrine of devils. Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law.
The law against eating flesh with the blood was given to Adam and is still in place with Noah; the word is true from the beginning.

The Most High requiring blood at the hand of every beast is animal sacrifice, still in place with Noah, passed down generation to generation. The judgment for sin has always been death. When Eve sinned and caused Adam to sin, either they had to die, or something had to stand in their place; the blood of the animal stood in for them. That is the scapegoat: it takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings, because they knew of the sacrifice from [Genesis 3](/bible/genesis/3).

Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: life for life. This law is way before Moses, so it cannot be dismissed as the law of Moses. The laws were never done away with; Christ came not to destroy the law but to fulfil, and not one jot or tittle passes from the law.

The covenant established here is with Noah, his seed, and every living creature: all flesh shall never again be cut off by the waters of a flood. This is a general covenant with all flesh. The covenant with Israel is found in [Jeremiah 31](/bible/jeremiah/31).

The bow in the cloud, the rainbow, is the token of the covenant between the Most High and the earth; it compasses the heaven about with a glorious circle, and His hands bended it. The world has taken that same bow, the token of the covenant, and turned it into the symbol of sodomy. The spiritual eyes will see what that means: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.
The waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. The next time the destruction is not water but fire, when the day of the Lord comes and the elements melt with fervent heat.

Shem, Ham, and Japheth went forth out of the ark and the whole earth was overspread from them. Ham dwelt in what is called Africa; Shem in the land mass toward Arabia; Japheth went into Europe. Ham is the father of Canaan, and Canaan dwelt in the land later called the land of Israel. That is how you know the land of Israel is a part of Africa; the maps separate Israel from Africa so that the connection is not made.

Noah was still perfect and righteous. A just man falleth seven times and riseth up again; one fall does not undo righteousness. Understand Noah's heart: he preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned. Strong drink is for him that is ready to perish and wine for those of heavy hearts; Noah drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High. Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; [Leviticus 18](/bible/leviticus/18) opens those laws.

Noah was asleep, so how did he know what his younger son had done? The Most High speaks to man in a dream, in a vision of the night, and reveals His secret unto His servants the prophets; Noah was a preacher of righteousness, and the Lord told him. Cursed be Canaan: a servant of servants unto his brethren. Blessed be the Lord God of Shem: it was revealed that the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem.

verses.text: And the whole earth was of one language, and of one speech.
And it came to pass, as they journeyed from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar; and they dwelt there.
And they said one to another, Go to, let us make brick, and burn them throughly. And they had brick for stone, and slime had they for morter.
And they said, Go to, let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.
And the Lord came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men builded.
And the Lord said, Behold, the people is one, and they have all one language; and this they begin to do: and now nothing will be restrained from them, which they have imagined to do.
Go to, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.
So the Lord scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city.
Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the Lord did there confound the language of all the earth: and from thence did the Lord scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.
And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.
Moreover, the nations in their wicked conspiracy being confounded, she found out the righteous, and preserved him blameless unto God, and kept him strong against his tender compassion toward his son.
Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?
The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the Lord, and against his anointed, saying,
Let us break their bands asunder, and cast away their cords from us.
He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: the Lord shall have them in derision.
